title: Unify backoff/credential config across Python/TS/Go SDKs and bump SDK versions
author: Aisha Khan
description:
Context: Multiple SDKs implemented slightly different default retry/backoff and credential refresh heuristics which has caused divergence in streaming reconnection behavior and customer confusion when swapping SDKs. This PR standardizes a small, explicit configuration surface and introduces a lightweight compatibility shim so older consumers keep current behavior unless they opt-in.

What this PR does: 1) Introduces an SDK-agnostic BackoffPolicy config (initial_ms, max_ms, factor, jitter_pct) and a CredentialRefreshWindow setting (refresh_before_expiry_ms) surfaced in Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs. 2) Adds a minimal cross-language bridge in the server-side compatibility layer so clients with legacy configs receive mappings to the new fields. 3) Normalizes stream resume behavior: clients will attempt token-refresh handshake up to N times with exponential backoff using the new policy; on permanent failures the runtime falls back to short HTTP polling (configurable) to avoid long stalls. 4) Bumps SDK versions: python -> 1.12.0, typescript -> 2.8.1, go -> v0.10.0. 5) Docs and migration guide added under docs/migration.

Why this approach: We observed three classes of issues in the wild: (a) aggressive retry loops under token expiry causing rate spikes, (b) mismatched jitter implementations making cross-SDK telemetry noisy, and (c) awkward developer ergonomics when configuring backoff separately per language. A small, explicit contract reduces customer friction and lets platform routing apply consistent policies.

Commits summary: - add: cross-sdk BackoffPolicy proto and mapping layer - feat(python): expose backoff and refresh_window in client config; bump 1.12.0 - feat(ts): unified config object and typed adapters; bump 2.8.1 - feat(go): backoff/cred bridge and context-aware stream manager; bump v0.10.0 - docs: migration guide, changelog, release note - test: add unit + e2e coverage for handshake jitter and fallback modes

Files changed (high level): sdk/python/redwood/client.py (expose backoff param), sdk/python/setup.py (version), sdk/typescript/src/config/backoff.ts (typed policy), sdk/typescript/package.json (version), sdk/go/stream/manager.go (credential window, backoff), sdk/go/go.mod (version), server/compat/credential_mapper.go (mapping layer), docs/migration/sdk-backoff-and-cred.md, ci/workflows/sdk-e2e.yml

Migration notes: Existing clients preserve behavior via the compatibility mapper; we recommend consumers set explicit BackoffPolicy and reduce refresh_window if they need more aggressive refresh. See docs/migration/sdk-backoff-and-cred.md for examples for each language.

Testing notes: unit tests added per SDK, plus an e2e matrix that runs streaming reconnect scenarios with token expiry simulated. Flaky integration test was stabilized by adding jitter clamp logic.

Release impact: non-breaking for typical users; opt-in for advanced backoff tuning. SDK package versions bumped so language package managers will see new releases.

release_notes: SDKs: Introduce a unified BackoffPolicy and CredentialRefreshWindow across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs. Normalizes streaming reconnect behavior and adds a compatibility mapper on the server to preserve legacy behavior. SDK version bumps: python 1.12.0, typescript 2.8.1, go v0.10.0. Non-breaking; users can opt-in to tune backoff/refresh settings.
migration_steps: 2) Update client construction to pass explicit BackoffPolicy if you rely on aggressive reconnects.
3) If you use custom token refresh logic, reduce refresh_window to avoid unnecessary re-auth attempts.
4) Pin new SDK versions in your dependency manager and run integration tests in a staging environment.
notes_for_customers: Most customers do not need to change code. If you observe reconnect storms around token rotation, set BackoffPolicy.initial_ms to a higher value and add jitter_pct to 0.2+. For high-throughput streaming, consider increasing batch windows together with BackoffPolicy to avoid token refresh amplification.
important_security_notes: Credential mapping is server-side and only adjusts configuration semantics; no secret material is stored by the mapper. Kept cryptographic flows unchanged. Security scan passed.
notes: This PR was coordinated with SDK leads for a simultaneous publish to PyPI/NPM/Go proxy. We allowed a short stabilization window after merge before pushing packages to avoid churn for early adopters.
